name: Authorised Push Payment Scams
description: Victims are deceived or coerced into authorising a payment to an account controlled by a criminal, often under a false pretext such as a safe-account request, a fake invoice or an invented purchase. Because the customer authorises the payment, controls rely on spotting behavioural change and mule receiving accounts.

sources.text: UK Finance, Annual Fraud Report (specify year, e.g. 2025)
Payment Systems Regulator, APP scams: Requirement for reimbursement, Policy Statement PS23/4 (Dec 2023) (see also PS23/3, June 2023; PS24/7, Oct 2024)
FATF, INTERPOL and Egmont Group, Illicit Financial Flows from Cyber-enabled Fraud (2023)

indicators.name: Payment to new payee under apparent time pressure
indicators.canon: Payment to new payee under apparent time pressure
indicators.desc: Victim-side: a first payment of unusually high value to a newly created payee, made quickly after a phone call or message and often outside normal patterns.
indicators.ctx: Victim-side: a first payment of unusually high value to a newly created payee, made quickly after a phone call or message and often outside normal patterns.
indicators.fp: Genuine house purchases, one-off large bills or planned gifts to new payees.
refs: UK Finance, Annual Fraud Report (published annually)

indicators.name: Customer on an active call while paying
indicators.canon: Customer on a live call while transacting
indicators.desc: Customer is on an active phone call, hesitant or following dictated instructions while depositing cash or making an online payment.
indicators.ctx: Victim-side: session signals show the customer is on a live phone call, navigating hesitantly, or following dictation during online banking.
indicators.fp: Customers legitimately on hand-free calls with family or advisers.
refs: UK Finance, Annual Fraud Report (published annually)

indicators.name: Evasive or scripted answers about payment purpose
indicators.canon: Unable or unwilling to explain transaction purpose or origin
indicators.desc: When asked about a transaction, the customer gives vague, rehearsed, inconsistent or shifting explanations of its purpose, source or counterparties.
indicators.ctx: Victim-side: when asked about the payment, the customer gives rehearsed, inconsistent or irritated answers, or says they were told to mislead the bank.
indicators.fp: Privacy-minded customers or those unsure of terminology.
refs: UK Finance, Annual Fraud Report (published annually)

indicators.name: Remote-access software present during banking session
indicators.canon: Remote-access, emulator or automation tools in session
indicators.desc: Remote-desktop, screen-sharing, emulator or scripted-control tools are detected during onboarding, login or payment sessions.
indicators.ctx: Victim-side: remote desktop or screen-sharing tools detected while the customer logs in or pays.
indicators.fp: IT support or family helping a customer with consent.
refs: UK Finance, Annual Fraud Report (published annually)

indicators.name: Sudden liquidation of savings or investments to fund payments
indicators.canon: Sudden liquidation of savings or assets
indicators.desc: Savings, investments or assets are sold abruptly, followed by withdrawal or transfer.
indicators.ctx: Victim-side: movement of long-held savings, fixed deposits or investments into the current account followed by outbound transfers.
indicators.fp: Home deposits, life events or planned purchases.
refs: UK Finance, Annual Fraud Report (published annually)

indicators.name: Beneficiary account name mismatch or no-match result
indicators.canon: Beneficiary account name mismatch or no-match result
indicators.desc: Victim-side: confirmation-of-payee check returns no match or close match and the customer proceeds regardless.
indicators.ctx: Victim-side: confirmation-of-payee check returns no match or close match and the customer proceeds regardless.
indicators.fp: Typos, trading names or joint accounts producing benign mismatches.
refs: UK Finance, Annual Fraud Report (published annually)

indicators.name: Receiving account rapidly forwards incoming credits
indicators.desc: Funds received into an account are forwarded onward within a very short period, often in near-equal amounts and leaving minimal balance.
indicators.ctx: Mule-side: funds credited by multiple unrelated individuals are moved out within minutes or hours to other accounts, cash or crypto.
indicators.fp: Pass-through for legitimate marketplace sellers or agents.
refs: UK Finance, Annual Fraud Report (published annually)

indicators.name: Receiving account is new or recently dormant with many unrelated senders
indicators.canon: Receiving account is new or recently dormant with many unrelated senders
indicators.desc: Mule-side: a recently opened or reactivated account receives payments from many unrelated people with narratives that do not fit the stated profile.
indicators.ctx: Mule-side: a recently opened or reactivated account receives payments from many unrelated people with narratives that do not fit the stated profile.
indicators.fp: Fundraising, club accounts or small traders with genuine many-to-one inflows.
refs: UK Finance, Annual Fraud Report (published annually)

indicators.name: Payment narrative or reference suggests safe-account or investment script
indicators.desc: Payment narratives or references contain wording linked to scams such as safe accounts or investment schemes.
indicators.ctx: Victim-side: references such as 'safe account', 'HMRC', 'fees' or crypto platform names appear alongside atypical transfers.
indicators.fp: Genuine references to tax or investment platforms.
refs: UK Finance, Annual Fraud Report (published annually)

indicators.name: Multiple prior scam alerts or repeat victimisation
indicators.canon: Multiple prior scam alerts or repeat victimisation
indicators.desc: Victim-side: the customer previously reported or was warned of fraud and is again sending payments to new payees.
indicators.ctx: Victim-side: the customer previously reported or was warned of fraud and is again sending payments to new payees.
indicators.fp: Customers who have since become aware and are genuinely transacting.
refs: UK Finance, Annual Fraud Report (published annually)
